However, the United States and United Kingdom conspicuously declined to sign it, citing concerns over regulatory overreach, national security, and competitiveness in AI innovation. This makes Statement I correct and Statement II incorrect, since US and UK did not sign, contrary to the statement's claim.
explanations: (a) Correct — only Statement I is accurate; the summit was co-chaired with India and built on prior Bletchley Park and Seoul summits, while US and UK did not sign the declaration.
(b) Incorrect — Statement II is false since US and UK abstained from signing the declaration.
(c) Incorrect — since Statement II is wrong, both cannot be correct.
(d) Incorrect — Statement I is factually correct, so 'neither' is wrong.
keyfact: Paris AI Action Summit 2025 (India co-chair) followed Bletchley Park (2023) and Seoul (2024); US and UK refused to sign the Paris declaration.
statements: I — Correct: The Paris AI Action Summit (Feb 2025) was co-chaired by France and India, continuing the series from Bletchley Park (2023) and Seoul (2024).
II — Incorrect: The US and UK refused to sign the Paris declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI, unlike most other participating nations.
summary: The correct answer is (a) 1 only. The Paris AI Action Summit (Feb 2025) was indeed co-chaired by France and India and built on the Bletchley Park (UK, 2023) and Seoul (2024) summits, but the US and UK notably refused to sign the joint declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.

ocr: Consider the following pairs : International Year of the : 2026 I. Woman Farmer International Year of te 2027 is Sustainable and Resilient Tourism International Year of Peace : 2025 Ill. and Trust International Year of Asteroid : 2029 Awareness and Planetary Defence How many of the — given above are correctly matched (a) Only one (b) Only two (c) Only three (ad) All the four 41 [P.T.O.
subject: Science & Tech
detail: UN International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly (sometimes on the recommendation of ECOSOC or a specialised agency such as FAO or UNESCO) to draw global attention to a theme. This question tests recent UN-proclaimed observances, a favourite UPSC current-affairs area. The facts to hold are: 2025 is the International Year of Peace and Trust (also the Year of Quantum Science and Technology, and of Glaciers' Preservation); 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer (also Rangelands and Pastoralists, and Volunteers for Sustainable Development); 2027 is the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; 2029 is the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence, linked to the close approach of asteroid Apophis on 13 April 2029. Elimination logic: if a student knows even two pairs are right, options (a) and (b) are ruled out. Knowing three correct pairs leaves only (c) or (d), and the fourth pair, 2029 Apophis, is easily confirmed by its astronomical logic. In 'how many pairs' questions, check each pair independently, because UPSC often makes all items correct or all incorrect.
explanations: Wrong: it says only one pair is correct, but all four pairs match the UN proclamations.
Wrong: it says only two pairs are correct, but all four are correct, so the count is understated.
Wrong: it says only three pairs are correct, but the fourth pair (Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence, 2029) is also correct.

Correct: 2026 for the Woman Farmer, 2027 for Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, 2025 for Peace and Trust, and 2029 for Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence are all accurate, so all four pairs are correctly matched.
keyfact: 2025 Peace and Trust; 2026 Woman Farmer; 2027 Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; 2029 Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence (Apophis flyby, 13 April 2029).
option_notes: Only one: this would mean exactly one pair is right. It is a typical distractor in 'how many pairs' questions, designed to catch students who know just one observance. The UPSC convention is that each pair is judged independently, so counting carefully matters. Here the count is four, not one.

Only two: this would mean exactly two of the four pairs are right. It tempts students who confuse the years of the Woman Farmer (2026) and Tourism (2027), or who are unsure about Peace and Trust. Swapping years between the pairs would be the usual trap, but none of the years here is swapped.

Only three: this is the most tempting wrong option, because the 2029 Asteroid Year is the least familiar of the four. Students who doubt it as obscure or fictional would choose three. It is real: it is tied to the Apophis flyby on 13 April 2029, so the count is four.

All the four: this is the correct option. The 2025, 2026, 2027 and 2029 pairings all match UNGA proclamations. In such questions UPSC sometimes makes every item correct, so students should not assume that at least one pair has been altered.
related: 2023 was the International Year of Millets, proposed by India and adopted by the UNGA.
The asteroid Apophis will pass about 32,000 km from Earth on 13 April 2029.
NASA's DART mission (2022) changed the orbit of Dimorphos, a moonlet of the asteroid Didymos.
2025 is the 80th anniversary of the UN, founded on 24 October 1945.
UN Tourism, formerly UNWTO, is headquartered in Madrid.
International Asteroid Day is observed on 30 June.
15 October is the International Day of Rural Women.
International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly.
statements: I — Correct: The International Year of the Woman Farmer is 2026, proclaimed by the UNGA. It highlights women's role in agriculture and food security and the gaps they face in access to land, credit, technology and markets. FAO is expected to lead the observance. Women make up a large share of the agricultural workforce, especially in developing countries, yet hold a small share of land titles. 2026 also carries the Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.

II — Correct: The International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism is 2027, proclaimed by the UNGA. UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO, headquartered in Madrid) is the lead agency. The theme promotes tourism that is low-carbon, climate-resilient and inclusive, supports local communities, and contributes to the SDGs. World Tourism Day is observed on 27 September each year. Tourism is a major contributor to GDP and jobs, but it is vulnerable to climate shocks and pandemics.

III — Correct: The International Year of Peace and Trust is 2025, proclaimed by the UNGA on the initiative of Turkmenistan, which stresses trust-building, dialogue and cooperation between nations. 2025 also marks the 80th anniversary of the UN, founded on 24 October 1945. The year is linked to the UN Charter's aim of maintaining international peace and security. Other 2025 years include Quantum Science and Technology, and Glaciers' Preservation.

IV — Correct: The International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence is 2029, proclaimed by the UNGA. The asteroid 99942 Apophis, about 340 m across, will pass within roughly 32,000 km of Earth on 13 April 2029, closer than geostationary satellites. The year promotes awareness and international cooperation on near-Earth object detection and deflection. Related events include NASA's DART mission (2022), which altered the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos, and International Asteroid Day on 30 June.
summary: The answer is (d): all four pairs are correctly matched. The UN General Assembly has proclaimed 2025 as the International Year of Peace and Trust, 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer, 2027 as the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, and 2029 as the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence.
topic_notes: International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly to focus attention on issues of global concern. International Days are also set by the UNGA or by specialised agencies such as UNESCO, WHO and FAO. Some recent and upcoming International Years: 2023 was the International Year of Millets (proposed by India, and adopted by the UNGA in March 2021); 2024 was the International Year of Camelids; 2025 is the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, of Peace and Trust, and of Glaciers' Preservation (with the Decade of Action for Cryospheric Sciences 2025-2034); 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer, of Rangelands and Pastoralists, and of Volunteers for Sustainable Development; 2027 is the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; and 2029 is the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence. Apophis (99942) is an Aten-class near-Earth asteroid, and the OSIRIS-APEX mission is to study it in 2029. Planetary defence ties into NASA's DART mission, ESA's Hera mission and the UN-endorsed International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN) and Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG). Other relevant angles: UN Tourism is a specialised agency; FAO leads many agricultural years; UNESCO leads years in science and culture; the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs frame most of these themes. UPSC frequently pairs year and theme, or asks which agency leads the observance, so revise the lead agency along with each year. For the Woman Farmer year, also remember India's Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) under DAY-NRLM, and that 15 October is the International Day of Rural Women.

question: Consider the following statements with regard to BRICS : I. 16th BRICS Summit was held under the Chairship of Russia in Kazan. Il. Indonesia -has become a _ full member of BRICS. Ill. The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was Strengthening Multiculturalism for Just Global Development and Security. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) held its 16th Summit in October 2024 in Kazan, Russia, under Russia's chairship for that year — a key fact to remember since chairship rotates annually among members. At this summit, BRICS expanded further: Indonesia was invited and subsequently became a full member of BRICS, effective January 2025, joining earlier expansion additions like Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, and Saudi Arabia (invited). The official theme of the Kazan Summit was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security' — emphasizing multilateral cooperation, not 'multiculturalism' as wrongly stated in the question (a subtle but important distractor testing careful reading). Students must distinguish 'multilateralism' (cooperation among multiple states/institutions) from 'multiculturalism' (cultural diversity), as UPSC often tests such wording traps. Thus, statements I and II are factually accurate, while III contains a factual/terminological error, making (a) the correct choice.
explanations: (a) Correct — Statements I and II are both factually accurate regarding the Kazan Summit and Indonesia's membership.
(b) Incorrect — Statement III is wrong due to the 'multiculturalism' vs 'multilateralism' error; this combination wrongly includes III.
(c) Incorrect — This combination wrongly includes III (incorrect) and omits II (which is correct).
(d) Incorrect — This omits Statement II, which is factually correct, making it an incomplete answer.
keyfact: 16th BRICS Summit (2024) — Kazan, Russia; theme: 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'; Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025.
statements: I — Correct: The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan, Russia, in October 2024, under Russia's chairship.
II — Correct: Indonesia became a full member of BRICS, with membership taking effect in January 2025.
III — Incorrect: The actual theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', not 'Multiculturalism' as stated.
summary: The correct answer is (a) I and II. The 16th BRICS Summit (2024) was indeed held in Kazan, Russia under Russian chairship, and Indonesia was admitted as a full BRICS member (effective January 2025). Statement III is incorrect because the actual theme used the word 'Multilateralism', not 'Multiculturalism'.

question:
Consider the following statements about Lokpal :
I. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India. Il. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a Member of the Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory, and only the Chief Justice of India, whether incumbent or retired, has to be its Chairperson. Ill. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as the Chairperson or Member, as the case may be.
IV. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: None of the above statements is correct
subject: Polity
detail: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 establishes an anti-corruption ombudsman for the Union. Composition: a Chairperson and up to 8 Members (50% judicial), who must not be MPs/MLAs, and must be at least 45 years old on assuming office (Section 3) — this makes Statement III correct. The Chairperson need NOT be the CJI; he/she can be a former Chief Justice of India, or a former/sitting Judge of the Supreme Court, or an eminent person, making Statement II false. Jurisdiction extends to public servants, including those serving outside India if they are Indian citizens employed in connection with Union affairs (Section 14), making Statement I false. Regarding the PM, Lokpal CAN inquire into corruption allegations against a sitting PM, except matters relating to international relations, external/internal security, public order, atomic energy, and space — such inquiry requires a Full Bench decision with at least two-thirds majority and is held in camera, making Statement IV false. Thus only III is correct.
explanations: (a) Correct — Only Statement III accurately reflects the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 provisions; I, II, and IV are factually incorrect.
(b) Incorrect — Statement II is wrong since the Chairperson need not be the CJI; other eligible persons (former CJI, SC judge, eminent person) can also hold the post.
(c) Incorrect — Statement I is wrong as jurisdiction covers public servants posted outside India too; Statement IV is wrong as the PM can be inquired into with safeguards.
(d) Incorrect — This option wrongly claims none of the statements are correct, but Statement III is indeed accurate.
keyfact: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Chairperson/Member must be at least 45 years old, jurisdiction extends to officials outside India, and even a sitting PM can be probed (with safeguards).

statements.1: 1 — Incorrect: Lokpal's jurisdiction extends to public servants even when posted outside India, if they are in connection with affairs of the Union.

statements.2: 2 — Incorrect: The Chairperson can be a former CJI, a former/sitting SC Judge, or an eminent person; it need not be the CJI specifically.

statements.3: 3 — Correct: As per Section 3 of the Act, the Chairperson/Member must be at least 45 years of age on the date of assuming office.

statements.4: 4 — Incorrect: Lokpal can inquire into corruption allegations against a sitting PM, subject to certain safeguards (exclusions on sensitive subjects, Full Bench with two-thirds majority, in-camera proceedings).

summary: The correct answer is (a) – only Statement III is correct. Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Chairperson/Member must be at least 45 years old, but the other statements misrepresent the Act's provisions on jurisdiction and composition.

question:
Consider the following statements in respect of the first Kho Kho World Cup :
I. The event was held in Delhi, India.
II. Indian men beat Nepal with a score of 78-40 in the final to become the World Champion in men category. Ill. Indian women beat Nepal with a score of 54-36 in the final to become the World Champion in women category. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The inaugural Kho Kho World Cup 2025 was organised by the Kho Kho Federation of India and held in New Delhi from 13-19 January 2025, making statement I correct. In the men's final, India defeated Nepal, but the actual score was 54-36, not 78-40 as stated in statement II, making it incorrect. In the women's final, India also defeated Nepal, but the correct score was 78-40, not 54-36 as given in statement III, making it incorrect too. Essentially, the examiners swapped the scores between the men's and women's finals to create a plausible-looking but factually wrong pairing. Students must note India won both titles (men and women) in this event, but the exact numbers were interchanged in the statements, testing careful fact-recall rather than general awareness alone.
explanations: (a) Correct: Only statement I is accurate; II and III have swapped/incorrect scores.
(b) Incorrect: Both II and III contain wrong scores (swapped between categories).
(c) Incorrect: Statement III's score is wrong, so I and III together cannot be correct.
(d) Incorrect: Since II and III are both wrong, not all three statements can be correct.
keyfact: First Kho Kho World Cup 2025 held in New Delhi; India won both men's and women's titles, beating Nepal (men's final 54-36, women's final 78-40).
statements: I — Correct: The first Kho Kho World Cup 2025 was held in New Delhi, India.
II — Incorrect: India beat Nepal 54-36 (not 78-40) in the men's final.
III — Incorrect: India beat Nepal 78-40 (not 54-36) in the women's final; scores were swapped in the statement.
summary: The correct answer is (a) I only. The first Kho Kho World Cup 2025 was indeed held in New Delhi, India, but the final scores for both men's and women's categories as given in statements II and III are incorrect.

question:
Consider the following statements :
I. In the finals of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the world’s youngest winner after defeating the Russian player Ian Nepomniachtchi. Il. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world’s youngest ever Grandmaster. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: In 2024, two separate chess events are often confused: the 45th Chess Olympiad (a team event held in Budapest, Hungary, won by India's team including Gukesh) and the FIDE World Chess Championship match, where Gukesh Dommaraju defeated defending champion Ding Liren of China to become, at 18, the youngest ever undisputed World Chess Champion. Ian Nepomniachtchi, a Russian GM, was the opponent in the 2021 and 2023 World Championship matches against Magnus Carlsen/Ding Liren, not Gukesh's 2024 opponent. Hence Statement I conflates events and misnames the opponent, making it incorrect. Statement II is factually accurate: Abhimanyu Mishra, an American player of Indian origin, became the youngest Grandmaster in history in 2021 at age 12 years, 4 months and 25 days, breaking Sergey Karjakin's long-standing record. Students must distinguish 'Olympiad' (team, biennial) from 'World Championship' (individual title match) and remember key chess records and nationalities precisely, as UPSC often tests such factual overlaps.
explanations: (a) Incorrect — Statement I is factually wrong (wrong event/opponent), so 'I only' cannot be correct.
(b) Correct — Only Statement II is accurate; Statement I misstates the event and opponent.
(c) Incorrect — Since Statement I is false, 'Both I and II' is wrong.
(d) Incorrect — Statement II is true, so 'Neither I nor II' is wrong.
keyfact: Gukesh Dommaraju became the youngest World Chess Champion in 2024 by beating Ding Liren; Abhimanyu Mishra (USA) is the youngest-ever Grandmaster.
statements: I — Incorrect: Gukesh became World Chess Champion (not Olympiad winner in this context) in 2024 by defeating Ding Liren of China, not Ian Nepomniachtchi.
II — Correct: Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record for becoming the youngest-ever Grandmaster (2021, age 12 years 4 months).
summary: The correct answer is (b) II only. Statement I is wrong because Gukesh Dommaraju became the youngest World Chess Champion in 2024 by defeating China's Ding Liren, not by winning the Chess Olympiad and not against Nepomniachtchi; Statement II about Abhimanyu Mishra is correct.

question: Which one of the following Carnatic music 4, ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in Hindustani music ?
subject: Art & Culture
detail: Hindustani music classifies ragas into ten thaats under the Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande system, and Bilawal is the thaat taken as the basic 'shuddha' (natural) scale. It uses Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni, all shuddha, and corresponds to the Western major (Ionian) scale. Carnatic music uses the 72 melakarta scheme attributed to Venkatamakhin and later systematised in the Katapayadi form. The 29th melakarta, Dheera Shankarabharanam (Sankarabharanam), has Shadja, Chatushruti Rishabha, Antara Gandhara, Shuddha Madhyama, Panchama, Chatushruti Dhaivata and Kakali Nishada. This matches the Bilawal notes exactly. Elimination: Nat Bhairavi is the Carnatic name linked to Hindustani Asavari/Natabhairavi (Aeolian, the natural minor), with flat Ga, Dha and Ni. Kamavardhini (Pantuvarali, 51st melakarta) has Ri1, Ga3, Ma2, so it matches Hindustani Poorvi. Hanumatodi (8th melakarta) has Ri1, Ga2, Da1, Ni2 and corresponds to Bhairavi thaat. So only (d) is the major scale.
explanations: Incorrect: Nat Bhairavi corresponds to the natural minor scale (Hindustani Asavari thaat), with komal Ga, Dha and Ni, not Bilawal.
Incorrect: Kamavardhini (Pantuvarali) has Ri1 and Ma2 (tivra Ma), so it matches Hindustani Poorvi thaat, not Bilawal.
Incorrect: Hanumatodi (Todi) has komal Re, Ga, Dha and Ni, so it corresponds to Hindustani Bhairavi thaat, not Bilawal.
Correct: Dheera Shankarabharanam, the 29th melakarta, has all the notes of Bilawal (S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3), matching the Western major scale.
keyfact: Hindustani Bilawal = Carnatic Dheera Shankarabharanam (29th melakarta), the major scale.
option_notes: Nat Bhairavi is a Carnatic raga (Janya of the 20th melakarta Natabhairavi) whose scale resembles the Hindustani Asavari thaat and the Western natural minor. It has Sa, Ri2, Ga2, Ma1, Pa, Da1, Ni2. It is a popular raga in the Carnatic repertoire and used in light and film music, with a serious, devotional mood.

Kamavardhini is the 51st melakarta, better known as Pantuvarali. Its notes are S R1 G3 M2 P D1 N3, using a tivra Madhyama. Its Hindustani counterpart is Poorvi thaat. It is an evening raga with a deep, serious mood, and a janya of the Rudra chakra group, with Muthuswami Dikshitar composing in it.

Hanumatodi is the 8th melakarta (Todi in Hindustani usage, though the Hindustani Todi thaat differs). Its notes are S R1 G2 M1 P D1 N2. It corresponds to Bhairavi thaat and is a major, elaborate raga in the Carnatic system. It has a pathos-laden character and is performed as a main piece in concerts.

Dheera Shankarabharanam is the 29th melakarta, commonly called Sankarabharanam. Its notes are S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3, equal to the Western major scale and Hindustani Bilawal. It is one of the most important Carnatic ragas, a favourite of Tyagaraja and others. It is a sampoorna raga that is also the parent of many janya ragas.
related: Bilawal is the 'shuddha' thaat of Bhatkhande's ten-thaat system.
Dheera Shankarabharanam is the 29th melakarta.
Carnatic has 72 melakartas in 12 chakras of 6 each.
Mayamalavagowla (15th melakarta) corresponds to Hindustani Bhairav.
Mechakalyani (65th) corresponds to Hindustani Kalyan (Yaman).
Harikambhoji (28th) corresponds to Hindustani Khamaj.
Natabhairavi (20th) corresponds to Hindustani Asavari.
Purandara Dasa is called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music.
summary: The answer is (d) Dheera Shankarabharanam, so the unofficial key is correct. Raga Bilawal is the Hindustani 'Shuddha' scale (Bilawal thaat) with all natural notes, and its Carnatic equivalent is the 29th melakarta, Dheera Shankarabharanam, which has the same notes (S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S).
topic_notes: Indian classical music has two traditions, Hindustani (north) and Carnatic (south), sharing swaras but differing in classification and treatment. Hindustani ragas are grouped into ten thaats by V.N. Bhatkhande: Bilawal, Khamaj, Kafi, Asavari, Bhairavi, Bhairav, Kalyan, Marwa, Poorvi and Todi. Carnatic music uses the 72 melakarta (parent) ragas, arranged into 12 chakras of six ragas each, with the Katapayadi sutra giving the number from the name. Janya ragas derive from melakartas. The first 36 melakartas use Shuddha Madhyama (Ma1) and the last 36 use Prati Madhyama (Ma2). Key equivalents: Bilawal is Dheera Shankarabharanam (29), Kalyan is Mechakalyani (65), Khamaj is Harikambhoji (28), Kafi is Kharaharapriya (22) (approx., Kafi is also linked to Anandabhairavi), Asavari is Natabhairavi (20), Bhairavi is Hanumatodi (8), Bhairav is Mayamalavagowla (15), Poorvi is Kamavardhini or Pantuvarali (51), Marwa is Gamanashrama (53), and Todi is Subhapantuvarali (45). Carnatic music has the kriti as the major form, with the trinity Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. Purandara Dasa is called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music. Hindustani has dhrupad, khayal, thumri and tappa forms. Tansen of Akbar's court and Amir Khusrau are notable figures. Other angles to know are the 22 shrutis, the saptak, vadi and samvadi, and rasas.

question: The artificially fixed rupee-sterling exchange rate prescribed by the Hilton-Young Commission (1926) was adopted by the British Government for which one of the following reasons ?
options: Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India’s creditworthiness
Encouraging export of cotton produce from India 5
Preventing depreciation of the Rupee in terms of gold
subject: Economy
detail: The Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (Hilton-Young Commission, 1926) was set up to resolve the 'ratio controversy' - whether the rupee should be pegged at 1s 4d or 1s 6d to the pound sterling. It recommended 1s 6d, an overvalued rate compared to the pre-war 1s 4d, and adopted a gold-exchange standard. This high rate was favoured by the colonial government because Britain remitted large sums from India every year as 'Home Charges' (pensions, interest on sterling debt, administrative expenses in London) - a higher rupee value meant fewer rupees were needed to purchase the same sterling amount, easing the burden of remittance and helping India service its external debt, thus preserving its creditworthiness in London money markets. Indian industrialists and exporters (especially cotton/textile interests) opposed this rate since an overvalued rupee made Indian exports costlier and imports (including British manufactured goods) cheaper, hurting domestic industry - the opposite of options (b) and (c). Option (d) is incorrect as the issue was rupee-sterling parity, not gold parity per se, and depreciation vis-a-vis gold was not the stated rationale.
explanations: (a) Correct: The overvalued rate eased remittance of Home Charges to Britain and helped India maintain external creditworthiness for debt servicing.

(b) Incorrect: It did benefit importers incidentally (cheaper imports), but this was not the stated British objective; the real aim was remittance/creditworthiness, not aiding Indian importers as a policy goal.
(c) Incorrect: An overvalued rupee actually discouraged cotton and other exports by making them costlier abroad, the opposite of this option.
(d) Incorrect: The concern was rupee-sterling exchange stability under the gold-exchange standard, not preventing rupee depreciation against gold specifically.
keyfact: Hilton-Young Commission (1926) fixed rupee at 1s 6d to sterling to ease Britain's Home Charges remittances and preserve India's creditworthiness, hurting Indian exporters.
summary: The expected answer (a) is correct. The Hilton-Young Commission (1926) recommended the artificially high 1s 6d ratio primarily because it reduced the rupee cost of Britain's 'Home Charges'/remittances and helped India maintain external creditworthiness under the gold-exchange standard.

note: This image may contain more than one question. Answer Q3.
ocr: The artificially fixed rupee-sterling exchange rate prescribed by the Hilton-Young Commission (1926) was adopted by the British Government for which one of the following reasons ? (a) Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India’s creditworthiness (b) Providing support to Indian importers (c) Encouraging export of cotton produce from India 5 (d) Preventing depreciation of the Rupee in terms of gold
subject: Economy
detail: The Hilton-Young (Royal) Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926, fixed the rupee-sterling ratio at 1 shilling 6 pence, deliberately higher than the market-determined rate of roughly 1s 4d. This 'artificial' overvaluation was pushed by the British Government and favoured British financial and administrative interests: it made it cheaper, in rupee terms, to remit the large annual 'Home Charges' (pensions, interest on India's sterling debt, salaries of British officials, army costs) from India to Britain, and it reinforced confidence in India's external solvency/creditworthiness in London's capital markets, where India regularly borrowed. However, an overvalued rupee made Indian exports (notably raw cotton and other agricultural produce) dearer in foreign markets, hurting exporters and producers — exactly the opposite of option (c). It also hurt Indian industry generally by encouraging cheaper imports, not supporting importers in a protective sense as in (b). Option (d) is a circular/irrelevant restatement, not the policy rationale. This issue became a major nationalist grievance, with leaders like Purshottamdas Thakurdas and economists criticising the 1s6d ratio as sacrificing Indian economic interests for British fiscal convenience.
explanations: (a) Correct: overvaluation eased Home Charges remittances to Britain and bolstered India's creditworthiness in London markets — the real rationale behind the British government's choice.

(b) Incorrect: the policy affected importers favourably only incidentally (cheaper imports), but this was not the stated or primary purpose; it was not aimed at 'supporting Indian importers' as a policy goal.

(c) Incorrect: an overvalued rupee made Indian cotton exports costlier and less competitive abroad, actually discouraging rather than encouraging cotton exports — this is the opposite of the actual effect.
(d) Incorrect: this is not a meaningful independent 'reason'; the rupee's value was fixed relative to sterling/gold by policy choice, not as a defensive measure against depreciation in terms of gold.
keyfact: Hilton-Young Commission (1926) fixed rupee at 1s 6d, overvaluing it to ease Home Charges remittances and protect India's creditworthiness in London — at the cost of Indian exporters.
summary: The correct answer is (a), not (c) as given. The 1s 6d gold-exchange rate fixed by the Hilton-Young Commission (1926) overvalued the rupee, which eased the flow of 'Home Charges' remittances from India to Britain and kept India's external credit standing high in London money markets — it did not help cotton exports, which it actually hurt by making Indian goods costlier abroad.

subject: Economy
detail: The Hilton-Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926) recommended fixing the rupee at 1s 6d sterling (equivalent to 18d), rejecting the earlier 1s 4d ratio demanded by Indian merchants and industrialists. This overvaluation was controversial because it made Indian exports costlier and imports cheaper, harming Indian producers (especially of raw materials like cotton and jute) while benefiting British exporters to India. The key British rationale was financial: a higher, stable rupee value meant that the fixed sterling obligations India owed Britain—'Home Charges' (pensions, interest on debt, administrative costs paid in London)—could be remitted with fewer rupees, easing the burden on Indian finances from Britain's perspective and reassuring London bankers of India's ability to service debt, i.e., maintaining India's creditworthiness in international capital markets. Student should eliminate (b) since 'importers' were a side beneficiary, not the stated official rationale; (c) is opposite—exports were discouraged by overvaluation; (d) is a technical restatement unrelated to the actual policy motive of remittance/credit management.
explanations: Correct: The overvalued rupee reduced the rupee cost of remitting Home Charges to Britain and reassured international markets of India's fiscal credibility, which was the Government's real motive.
Incorrect: Indian importers benefited incidentally from a stronger rupee (cheaper imports), but this was not the stated British governmental rationale for fixing the rate.
Incorrect: The overvalued rupee actually discouraged, not encouraged, Indian cotton exports by making them costlier in foreign markets.
Incorrect: This is a vague technical restatement of the gold-linked fixing, not the substantive economic/political reason behind the British decision.
keyfact: Hilton-Young Commission (1926) fixed rupee at 1s 6d sterling mainly to ease remittance of Home Charges to Britain and preserve India's international creditworthiness, despite hurting Indian exporters.
summary: The correct answer is (a), not (b). The overvalued rupee-sterling ratio (1 rupee = 1s 6d) fixed by the Hilton-Young Commission made it cheaper for the British Government to transfer Home Charges and other remittances from India to Britain, and helped maintain India's credit standing in international markets; it did not specifically aid Indian importers as a policy objective.

(d) Incorrect: The fixed ratio was about rupee-sterling exchange, not directly about preventing rupee depreciation against gold; gold standard link was a separate issue, and this wasn't the Commission's primary justification.

This overvaluation served British financial and imperial interests: it reduced the rupee cost of the 'Home Charges'—payments India made to Britain for interest on debt, pensions, and administrative expenses, which were fixed in sterling—and it bolstered confidence among London investors and creditors regarding India's ability to service sterling obligations, i.e., its creditworthiness.
